reason: Verified. In state=day (paper and record rooms too) backMeasure reuses the forward row() builder, so all eight past rows carry the hidden unit " days away," under a "days back" heading: a screen reader hears "14 days away" for 19 September, already past. Partly wrong, though - the unit is screen-reader-only, not visible, and the gate's row-unit assertion runs on state=phone, which has no past rail, so it certifies nothing here.
sharpenedFix: Pass a direction/unit into row() so backMeasure renders "days back," in .b-unitSaid. Also fix closeRun() in place(), which rewrites that same span (" days away, first of N moments") and runs over .b-back via the line-1352 sweep - otherwise the wrong word returns on repaint. Keep the trailing comma: the span is clipped, so it never reads as a stray fragment, and the comma is what makes the spoken row a sentence. Extend the gate with a state=day assertion that each row's unit matches its rail's direction; the phone-state check at line 289 cannot see the past rail.
